summary.en: The historic and cultural heart of Rock Springs, this area offers a raw, authentic look into a Western coal town forged by industry, immigration, and conflict.

description.en: Housed in the imposing, castle-like former City Hall, this museum offers a crucial look at the 1885 Rock Springs Massacre and the town's complex cultural fabric.
A hidden gem inside the 1910 Carnegie Library, this gallery holds a nationally significant collection of American art, including works by Norman Rockwell and Grandma Moses.
Wander the historic streets to spot faded, hand-painted advertisements from a century ago and admire varied architectural styles that tell the story of a boom-and-bust town.
